name: db-rest
what_it_holds: A live REST API wrapper (now built on db-vendo-client after DB's HAFAS API was retired) exposing Deutsche Bahn station search, timetable, and journey-planning data at v6.db.transport.rest.
why_useful: A lightweight live-query method for current DB schedules/stations if a point-in-time snapshot approach (repeated pulls) were wanted; no historical store of its own, so lower value than piebro/deutsche-bahn-data for backtesting.
themes: Rail and ground travel: Amtrak ridership, SNCF/DB/Trenitalia open data, Eurostar, bus (FlixBus), rideshare datasets (Uber Movement), NYC TLC airport trips, Chicago taxi
why_all: A lightweight live-query method for current DB schedules/stations if a point-in-time snapshot approach (repeated pulls) were wanted; no historical store of its own, so lower value than piebro/deutsche-bahn-data for backtesting.

name: rand-net/visa-cli
what_it_holds: 24-star Python CLI tool (updated 13 Sep 2026, MIT) that queries the ilyankou/passport-index-dataset to look up visa requirements between any two countries; a thin client, not a new dataset.
why_useful: Confirms the ilyankou dataset is actively used/maintained (recency signal); the CLI itself has no independent data value beyond that pointer.
themes: Cross-border and visa data: Schengen visa statistics, ESTA, ETIAS, CBP wait times, passport index, border crossings BTS
why_all: Confirms the ilyankou dataset is actively used/maintained (recency signal); the CLI itself has no independent data value beyond that pointer.

name: gasbuddy-mcp-price-tracker
what_it_holds: An MCP (Model Context Protocol) server (1 star, updated 22 Apr 2026, MIT) that lets an LLM tool-call gasbuddy.com for cheapest station prices by city/zip; no stored data.
why_useful: Marginal: shows another live-query path into GasBuddy but adds nothing over py-gasbuddy for building a time series; flagged mainly for completeness under 'methods/tooling'.
themes: Road travel and fuel: gas prices (EIA, AAA), vehicle miles travelled, holiday driving, toll data
why_all: Marginal: shows another live-query path into GasBuddy but adds nothing over py-gasbuddy for building a time series; flagged mainly for completeness under 'methods/tooling'.

name: sosedoff/opentable
what_it_holds: Ruby client wrapping OpenTable's (unofficial) restaurant-search and reservation-availability endpoints; 142 stars, updated 2026-08-15, no data committed, license 'other' (check terms before use).
why_useful: A live client for pulling current OpenTable restaurant availability/booking data (a real-time seated-diners/leisure-demand proxy, gap #6) rather than a historical panel; would need to be run going forward to build a time series, and ToS for automated pulls from OpenTable is a human call per repo rules.
themes: Restaurant and leisure proxies: OpenTable state of the industry CSV, Yelp dataset, Google Maps reviews scrapers, event ticket data
why_all: A live client for pulling current OpenTable restaurant availability/booking data (a real-time seated-diners/leisure-demand proxy, gap #6) rather than a historical panel; would need to be run going forward to build a time series, and ToS for automated pulls from OpenTable is a human call per repo rules.

name: omarshahine/restaurant-cli
what_it_holds: Pluggable CLI/agent-skill for booking restaurant reservations across Resy, OpenTable, Tock, SevenRooms from one codebase; 8 stars, MIT, updated 2026-09-02.
why_useful: Marginal: built for booking, not data collection, but the same API-plugin layer could in principle be adapted to poll availability across multiple reservation platforms as a leisure-demand proxy; flagged as a low-confidence lead only.
themes: Restaurant and leisure proxies: OpenTable state of the industry CSV, Yelp dataset, Google Maps reviews scrapers, event ticket data
